title: firstmate's host record is never blanked or silently kept wrong: rounds never write it, an unknown detection marks it unconfirmed and says so on the board, and settled pre-T-151 decisions stop being listed as unacknowledged
acceptance: Why. Two session-record defects seen on 2026-10-04/05. (1) `state/session/host.json` has been found as `{"harness":null,...}` after it held `claude`, which makes the worker rule `opposite-of-host` fall back to the configured fallback head (bin/fm-config.sh:506-512) and send rounds to the wrong vendor. (2) Every `bin/fm-session.sh start`/`status` lists about 30 old captain decisions as unacknowledged (for example D-firstmate-workflow-T105-1 and T117-1 shown as `merge: running`, though their decision files say `merged`), so a real new decision is buried. This task closes both. It is items 7 and 8 of state/briefs/PLAN-2026-10-05-remaining-issues.md as revised after independent review.

The real writers of host.json, verified on main 7c9877e (there is no crew-side writer; the earlier claim that crew rounds run `fm-session.sh status` was wrong: skills/firstmate/dispatch-crew/SKILL.md:38 is firstmate's own instruction). Exactly two code paths write it: (a) bin/lib/fm_host.py:81 (`save(state/session/host.json, collect(root))`), called by bin/fm-session.sh:31 on every `start` and `status`; `collect()` (:49-63) stores `harness=detect()` from bin/lib/fm_hooks.py:144-159, and `detect()` returns None when FM_HARNESS is unset, `life.session_owner()` raises (for example 'no session found: every ancestor up to pid 1 is a launcher', seen tonight from lifeline-launched processes) or names a non-harness process, and CLAUDECODE is not '1'; so any `start`/`status` run from such a context overwrites a good record with null. (b) bin/fm-session.sh:32-44, which after any fm_host.py failure (missing file, import error, crash) writes the literal null record over whatever was there. Callers of `fm-session.sh status` include firstmate's manual turns (bin/lib/fm_hooks.py:305 guidance, skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:120) and any hook or script that runs it. Readers: bin/fm-config.sh:467-474 `fm_host_harness` (used by `fm_role_vendor` :503-515 and `fm_record_vendor_resolution` :520-528), board/server.ts:606-621 `firstmateHost` (crew row :1156 and engine badge :335), and tests/lib/firstmate_host.py, tests/board-readiness.test.sh:69-111, tests/e2e/firstmate-host.spec.ts, tests/e2e/board-engine-rule.spec.ts.

Detection with a source. Add `detect_source()` to bin/lib/fm_hooks.py returning `(harness, source)` where source is 'env' (FM_HARNESS), 'owner' (the session owner process name matched a harness), 'claudecode' (CLAUDECODE=1) or None (unknown). `detect()` keeps its signature and returns `detect_source()[0]`, so its other callers (fm_hooks.py install/status paths) are unchanged. No new Codex environment marker is added: a positive Codex detection stays FM_HARNESS or the owner process name, because no Codex-set variable has been verified from a real Codex session (a stub must answer like the vendor; inventing one is out of scope).

Session identity. fm_host.py records the writer's session as `session: {pid, started}` where pid is `fm_lifeline.session_owner()` and `started` is that process's start time read with `ps -p <pid> -o lstart=` (works on macOS and Linux), or `session: null` when session_owner raises. It also records `source` (from detect_source) and `written_by: {pid: os.getpid(), parent_command: the first 200 characters of the parent process command line}` so the next unexpected write can be traced. Existing fields `harness`, `cli_version`, `model`, `model_source` keep their names and meaning.

Write rules in fm_host.py (one function, e.g. `decide(previous, detected)`, unit-tested directly): (1) Positive detection (source not None): write the full record with `confirmed: true`, replacing any previous record, including a different harness (this is how a captain who switches firstmate from Claude to Codex updates it). (2) Unknown detection and no previous record, or a previous record whose harness is null: write the record as today with harness null, `confirmed: false`. (3) Unknown detection and a previous record with a non-null harness: never write null. If the current session identity is known and equals the previous record's `session`, leave the file byte-identical (same session, nothing learned). Otherwise rewrite the previous record's harness, cli_version, model and model_source unchanged, with `confirmed: false`, `unconfirmed_since` (ISO time, kept from the previous record if it was already unconfirmed), and `last_unknown: {session, written_by}`; the previous `session`, `source` and `written_by` are kept. A legacy record without `confirmed` is treated as confirmed.

Round guard and the fallback writer. bin/fm-session.sh:30 skips the host refresh entirely, writing nothing and printing nothing to stdout, when FM_IN_ROUND (set for every sandboxed round, bin/fm-sandbox.sh:335) or FM_RUN_DIR (set for every crew run, bin/fm-herdr.py:1484) is non-empty. The fallback at :32-44 no longer overwrites an existing host.json: if one exists it is left byte-identical and the existing warning 'host refresh failed; firstmate host is unknown' becomes 'host refresh failed; keeping the recorded host <harness or unknown>'; only when no record exists does it write the null record as today.

Saying it loudly. (a) `fm-session.sh start` and `status` print to stderr, when the record has `confirmed: false` and a non-null harness: `fm-session: firstmate host record is unconfirmed: it says <harness> (recorded <time> by session <pid>); this session could not detect its own harness. Run with FM_HARNESS=<claude|codex> bin/fm-session.sh status to confirm it.` (b) `fm_role_vendor` in bin/fm-config.sh, when resolving `opposite-of-host` from an unconfirmed record, adds one stderr line `fm-vendor: opposite-of-host: recorded host <harness> is unconfirmed since <time>` and still uses that harness (the rule's result does not change; no round is refused). (c) The board: board/server.ts `firstmateHost` (:606-621) adds `host_confirmed` (false only when the record says `confirmed: false`; true for a legacy record) to the crew row; the `Crew` type at board/server.ts:144 gains `host_confirmed?: boolean`, and the crew-row field list at :1356 includes it. board/public/ship.js copies it in the field-by-field crew rebuild at :222-249 (next to `host_recorded: !!a.host_recorded` at :238; a missing `host_confirmed` stays undefined so a legacy record shows no warning), and in both places the firstmate vendor is rendered (crew card `cvendor` :176-182 and roster `rv` :500-504) shows the vendor with a `warn` class and the localized text from a new key `hostUnconfirmed` ('{vendor} (unconfirmed)' / '{vendor}（未確認）') when `host_confirmed === false`. Today `warn` is styled only for the model cells (board/public/ship.css:395 `.crewcard dd.cmodel.warn`, :421 `.roster .rm.warn`), so board/public/ship.css adds `.crewcard dd.cvendor.warn` and `.roster .rv.warn` with the same declarations (`color:#e0967d;font-weight:650`), beside those two rules. The key is added to i18n/ui.en.json and i18n/ui.zh-TW.json; zh-CN derives through i18n/tw2cn.tsv as for every other key. No new event type is added, so bin/fm-diagram.sh is untouched.

Legacy receipts stay read-only. `unacknowledged()` in bin/fm-herdr.py:2005-2032 still never writes: no acknowledgement is recorded for any receipt, and nothing under state/session/observed/ is edited, moved or deleted. Change only the loop at :2014-2018 that reads receipts the retired watcher wrote before T-151: for each receipt, read the current decision `record_root(root)/state/decisions/<id>.json` (the same directory the board answers into for that root). If that file is missing or unreadable, list the receipt as today (this keeps tests/session.test.sh:714-717, where D-046 has no decision file). If it exists, use the current decision's fields (not the receipt's frozen copy) for the listing, and skip the receipt as settled when the current decision has `chosen` set and either (i) `kind == 'merge'`, `merge == 'merged'` and `merge_settled` is set, or (ii) the decision's task has a `merged` or `closed` event row carrying that `task` in `record_root(root)/state/events.jsonl` and no later captain `reopened` event for that task (the same reopening rule as board/server.ts:245-248: actor captain with a non-empty reason). Anything else (unanswered, a merge still running, `failed`, a task with no terminal event such as D-SK-001's SK-001) stays listed with its current state. Wake-queue items (`wakes(root)`) are not filtered by this rule. `wake_wait` and the `status` report keep calling the same function.

Tests (workers do not run the suites; evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates). Change tests/lib/firstmate_host.py in place: the collector-failure loop at about :155-180 now asserts that with `previous == 'claude'` the record is byte-identical after the failure and stderr says 'keeping the recorded host claude', and with no previous record the null record is written as today. Add cases there (fixtures that need a known or different session set FM_SESSION_PID, because the fixture env's FIRSTMATE_CI_SESSION=1 makes session_owner() return pid 1, bin/lib/fm_lifeline.py:247-252; the detect stub at about :189-191 follows the switch to detect_source()): unit tests of `decide()` for rules (1)-(3) including a switch claude->codex on positive detection, same-session unknown leaving the file byte-identical, different-session unknown producing `confirmed: false` with harness kept and `unconfirmed_since` preserved on a second unknown write; `FM_IN_ROUND=1 fm-session.sh status` and `FM_RUN_DIR=<dir> fm-session.sh status` leave an existing record byte-identical; the unconfirmed stderr line from `fm-session.sh status`; `fm_role_vendor worker` with an unconfirmed claude record prints `codex` and the unconfirmed line. Migration of today's record: `decide()` given a legacy previous record `{"harness":"claude","cli_version":...,"model":...,"model_source":...}` (no `confirmed`, no `session`) and an unknown detection produces `confirmed: false`, keeps harness claude and the other three fields, and sets `unconfirmed_since`; given the same legacy record and a positive detection it writes `confirmed: true`; `fm_role_vendor worker` with that legacy record prints `codex` and no 'unconfirmed' line. A legacy receipt whose task has a later captain `reopened` event after its `merged` event stays listed. Add to tests/session.test.sh: a legacy receipt for a merge decision whose decision file says merged with merge_settled is not listed; one whose task has a `merged` event is not listed; one whose decision is unanswered is listed with its current fields; one with no decision file is listed (existing D-046 case unchanged); and after `status` the observed/ and acknowledged/ directories are byte-identical. Add to tests/e2e/firstmate-host.spec.ts, for en and zh-TW: a record with `confirmed: false` shows the firstmate vendor cell with `warn` and the localized '(unconfirmed)' text, and a legacy record without the field shows no warning. Fail-first is expected from tests/firstmate-host.test.sh (firstmate_host.py), tests/session.test.sh and the e2e spec.

Docs, edited in place in their home sections (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md): design/design.md §4 '### Firstmate host and worker vendor (T-174)' (lines about 117-135): add the round guard, the never-null-over-known rule, `confirmed`/`unconfirmed_since`, `session`/`source`/`written_by`, and where unconfirmed is shown. The same paragraph is mirrored in skills/firstmate/SKILL.md (about 1108-1120) and README.md (about 316-330): update both to the same text. design/design.md §11 'Self-update', subsection '### Owners and wakes (T-151)' (heading at about :2678), the sentence at about :2780-2781 'Observations the retired watcher wrote under state/session/observed/ are still read.': extend it with the settled-receipt rule and that the read never writes.

In flight and migration. No migration step: today's host.json (`{"harness":"claude",...}` without `confirmed`) is read as confirmed and is replaced at the next positive detection. Rounds already running are unaffected (they read the record; this task changes only how it is written and displayed). The 30 legacy receipts listed today drop to those still open on the first `status` after the merge, with no file written. Ordering and overlap: plan item T-200 (autopilot and board reload) also edits bin/fm-session.sh and bin/fm-herdr.py; it is dispatched only after this task merges. Tasks T-196 (CI coverage), T-197 (cursor) and T-199 (worker notes) do not touch these files except tests/**; this task merges only after T-196 and is rebased onto it.
